shadows.statement: The build contains zero box-shadow declarations. Depth is carried by a three-step field ladder (paper, paper-2, surface), 1px hairlines and 2px ink wayfinding rules. This is a deliberate invariant, not an omission: a shadow would imply an object floating above a printed page.

devices.name: wayfinding rule
devices.purpose: Marks a genuine boundary: section top, table head, previous/next seam.

devices.name: scroll mask
devices.purpose: The only soft edge; signals that a scrollable strip continues.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The single authored easing curve, used for every state transition.

motion.name: quick
motion.purpose: Colour and background state transitions: hover, focus, link fills.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: Pip fill and border-colour settling on the rail.

motion.name: draw-line
motion.purpose: The line draws itself down to the current station on arrival; scaleY(0) to scaleY(1), transform-origin top.

motion.name: draw-line-delay
motion.purpose: Per-station stagger so the line arrives in reading order; stations 5+ share 360ms.

motion.name: land-pip
motion.purpose: The active pip arrives last: paper fill becomes signal, line border becomes ink.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion keeps the design and drops the theatre.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Masthead nav stops scrolling and drops its mask fade; board header row appears; previous/next split into two columns.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: The rail returns to a vertical 256px sticky column; below this it is a horizontal scrollable line diagram.

breakpoints.name: xl
breakpoints.purpose: The station index appears as a 248px right column (208px content after 40px padding).

breakpoints.name: shell
breakpoints.purpose: Maximum shell width for masthead, route strip and rail layout.

breakpoints.name: reader
breakpoints.purpose: Maximum width of the reading page, keeping the 64ch measure centred.

narrative.overview:
GoWiki is drawn as the instrument room of a transit authority: a schematic in hairlines on paper, a line that names every stop, and one lamp that says where you are standing. Every mark on the page is an address or a direction — a station number, a pip on the line, a citation that names the section it came from. The surface should look *issued* rather than *styled*, the way a printed timetable looks set rather than designed: paper ground, an enamel-blue header field, condensed signage capitals for anything that names a place, and a serif reading column for anything that explains one.

Density is high and volume is low. Many quiet 1px hairlines carry structure, so almost nothing needs to shout: the largest ink in the system is a condensed display line, and the loudest colour is a single yellow lamp that appears on three elements at most. Corners are square down to the last token. There are no shadows anywhere in the build — depth is a matter of which field a thing sits on, not how far it floats above the page.

The world deliberately rejects the documentation-site default it could have become: grey sidebar, rounded cards, soft drop shadows, a gradient hero, a pill-shaped tag. It rejects them because a generated wiki that looks hand-assembled contradicts the product's central claim — that every sentence has a machine-addressable source. The instrument metaphor is the argument.
keyCharacteristics: Square by default: every radius token (`--radius-sm` through `--radius-4xl`) resolves to 0px, and the station pip is a square inside a square.
Paper ground with an enamel header field; white is a *raised* surface, never the page.
Signal yellow (#f5c518) is a lamp, not a brand colour: current station, keyboard focus, and a status that needs attention.
One line hue per repository, resolved through `data-line` into `--line` and `--line-ink`, never written into markup.
Depth without shadow: 1px hairlines, field changes, and 2px ink rules.
One authored motion — the rail line drawing itself to the current station — plus 140ms and 240ms state transitions.

rules.name: The Signal Reservation Rule
rules.body: Signal yellow marks exactly three classes of thing: where you are (the active pip, the current destination, `::selection` on the text you have claimed), where the keyboard is (the focus ring on enamel, the skip link), and a state that asks for you now (the `Not connected` stamp, the signal button). It is never a hover fill on a neutral control, never a heading accent, never a decorative wash — a lamp that is always on is not a lamp.

rules.name: The Line Hue Identity Rule
rules.body: A repository's hue is assigned by hash and expressed only as `--line` / `--line-ink` through `data-line`. Fills use the field value; text, underlines, and bullet marks use the ink value. No component writes a hue as a literal, and no page picks a hue to look nice.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: The reading column is 64ch and stays 64ch. It is not stretched to fill a wide monitor and not widened for tables; a 66ch figure that appeared in an early brief is retired — 64ch is the printed line length the page is typeset to, and the side column leaves the layout before the measure would ever shrink.

rules.name: The Signage–Serif Split Rule
rules.body: Barlow Condensed names things, Source Serif 4 explains them, JetBrains Mono addresses them. The one deliberate exception is the station-index label, set in serif because it is the section's own prose title, not a place name — everything else that navigates is signage.

rules.name: The One Address Rule
rules.body: Every section has exactly one number, and the margin owns it. Author-typed numerals are stripped from headings on render, and the station index and the citation both read from the same heading parse — so the address printed in the margin and the address quoted in an answer can never disagree.

rules.name: The Rail-Before-Content Rule
rules.body: Navigation is drawn, not hidden. The rail is present at every width: vertical and sticky above 1024px, horizontal and scrollable below it. There is no state in which a reader cannot see the line they are on.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow implies an object floating above the page, and nothing here floats — every element is printed onto the paper. If a surface needs to read as raised, move it up the field ladder and give it a hairline, not a blur.

rules.name: The Field-Before-Border Rule
rules.body: Reach for a field change before a border. A row hover is a move to Chalk Surface; only genuine separations get a hairline, and only wayfinding gets a 2px rule.

rules.name: The Square-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Nothing is rounded — not tags, not buttons, not panels, not the pip. If a shape feels too sharp, the fix is spacing or a hairline, never a radius.

rules.name: The Border Weight Rule
rules.body: 1px divides, 2px addresses, 3px signals. There is no fourth weight: a hairline never thickens to look important, and a decorative rule never appears at all.

rules.name: The Cell-Not-Card Rule
rules.body: Containers are bordered cells on paper — hairline outline, square corners, no elevation. A card that floats above the page belongs to another product.

rules.name: The Next-Station Rule
rules.body: A reading page ends on previous/next station, not on a call to action. The primary action of a wiki page is the next thing to read, so it is never a button.

dos: Do hold the reading column at 64ch and move the side column out of the layout before the measure shrinks.
Do name places, controls, and counts in Barlow Condensed caps; explain them in Source Serif 4; address them in JetBrains Mono.
Do use `--line` / `--line-ink` through `data-line` for every repository hue, so light and dark modes both stay legible.
Do give every generated page the same station skeleton — index head, numbered sections, previous/next — so a reader learns the shape once.
Do build separation from 1px hairlines and field changes before reaching for any other device.
Do keep motion to the one arrival moment plus 140ms state transitions and 240ms pip fills, and honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do reserve signal yellow for current location, keyboard focus, text selection, and a status that needs attention.
Do preserve the focus outline at 2px with a 2px offset in every theme.
donts: Don't add `box-shadow`, `drop-shadow`, or any blur to imply elevation.
Don't round a corner on any surface you set — not buttons, tags, pips, panels, or code cells. (The browser's own focus ring and native scrollbar are outside the rule.)
Don't apply signal yellow as a hover fill on a control that was not already a signal field, as a heading accent, or as a decorative band.
Don't invent a sixth line hue or hard-code a hue in markup; assignment is deterministic per repository.
Don't use a gradient as a background fill; the only gradients permitted are the mask fades at the ends of scrollable strips.
Don't put a heading's number into the authored markdown — the margin owns the address and prints it once.
Don't turn the rail into a drawer, hamburger, or collapsed dropdown at any width.
Don't set a rail or board station name, or a control label, in serif — and don't set a paragraph in condensed caps.
Don't end a reading page with a primary button; the next station is the action.
Don't let a code sample push the page sideways — it scrolls inside its own window.
